name: Hermes
summary: Messenger of the gods and guide of souls to the Underworld. God of travelers, commerce, boundaries, and — notably — thieves and trickery, reflecting his own famously cunning infancy.
domain_role: Messages, travel, commerce, boundaries, thievery, guidance of souls (psychopomp)
origin_story: Son of Zeus and the nymph Maia, Hermes displayed his defining cunning almost immediately after birth: according to the Homeric Hymn to Hermes, he stole Apollo's sacred cattle on the very day he was born, cleverly disguising the animals' tracks, then talked his way out of trouble with wit rather than force — earning Apollo's grudging respect and a place among the Olympians.
achievements: Served as the official messenger of Zeus and the gods
Guided the souls of the dead to the Underworld as a psychopomp
Invented the lyre, which he later traded to Apollo
Patron of merchants, travelers, and — pointedly — thieves, reflecting his own trickster origins

signature_quote.text: The Homeric Hymn to Hermes frames his cattle theft on the day of his birth as the defining act establishing his character as a clever trickster god.
